previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, esophageal varices, and recent bladder tumor resection was admitted for evaluation of hematuria, gastrointestinal bleeding, and abdominal pain. He had a markedly elevated PSA of 99.2, prompting urology consultation and plans for a bone scan and outpatient initiation of casodex for suspected prostate cancer. During the hospitalization, he developed nausea and vomiting, which resolved after discontinuation of casodex and oxycodone, suggesting medication-related side effects. His renal function showed transient worsening, likely pre-renal due to dehydration, which improved with fluids. Imaging revealed mild colonic wall thickening consistent with chronic colopathy and a left ureteral stent without hydronephrosis. No active GI bleeding was observed during admission, and hemoglobin remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in urology and gastroenterology, and instructions to monitor kidney function and resume home medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with history of cirrhosis c/b grade 1 varices 
and portal hypertensive gastropathy, alcohol abuse c/b 
gastritis, and recent EGD/colonoscopy w/ colonic angioectasias 
(successfully treated w/ Argon therapy) who presented to ___ 
with complaints of chest and abdominal pain.

# Abdominal Pain: Recent EGD and colonoscopy (___) revealed 
gastritis, portal hypertensive gastropathy, colonic 
angioectasias (intervened upon), but no ulcers or active 
bleeding. Patient's LFTs were within normal limits with the 
exception of an isolated AST elevation to 70 in the setting of 
having ingested half a pint of hard liquor the day prior to 
admission. EtOH level 64 and lipase 69 on admission. The 
patient's abdomen was mildly tender to palpation diffusely but 
no rebound tenderness or guarding. He was treated conservatively 
with PPI and anti-nausea agents. He reported substantial 
improvement in his abdominal pain on HD#2 and endorsed that he 
wished to go home. He was subsequently discharged and cautioned 
regarding the risks of his heavy alcohol consumption.

# Anemia: Patient has a chronic anemia with Hgb on admission 
being 8.1. Believed to be due to chronic blood loss through a 
combination of significant hematuria (pt is s/p bladder tumor 
resection and has a ureteral stent in place), documented 
gastritis, and recently intervened upon colonic angioectasias. 
Reticulocyte count was inappropriately low at 2.1% (uncorrected) 
suggesting a failure of RBC production. He will need to follow 
up with his primary care doctor for ongoing workup of his 
anemia, including iron studies, B12/folate levels, and referral 
to a Hematologist if clinically indicated.

# Chest Pain: Patient endorsed chest pain on presentation to the 
ED. EKG was without ischemic changes and troponins were negative 
x2. His chest pain resolved without any specific treatment while 
he was in the ED.

==== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES =====

# Abdominal Pain:
- Continue to counsel patient regarding his alcohol use and its 
contribution to gastritis

# Anemia:
- Patient has been instructed to schedule a follow up 
appointment with his primary care doctor, at which time he 
should have ongoing workup of his anemia
- Recommend obtaining iron studies, B12/folate levels, and 
referral to a Hematologist if clinically indicated
- Recommend obtaining repeat CBC at time of follow up to ensure 
that his hemoglobin has not significantly downtrended from the 
value at time of discharge which was 8.0.
